name: Moses and the uncircumcised son
charge: Neglecting the token of the covenant in his own house, on the road to demand the release of God’s firstborn
summary: Sent back to Egypt with the rod of God in his hand and the message that Israel was the Lord’s son, his firstborn, whom Pharaoh must release or lose his own firstborn, Moses went with his wife and his sons. On the way, at the inn, the Lord met him and sought to kill him, because his own son was uncircumcised. Zipporah took a sharp stone and circumcised the child, and the Lord let him go. The laws did not begin at Sinai, and the covenant of circumcision still stands.
offenseFull: Circumcision was not a Sinai ordinance. It was given to Abraham as the token of the covenant: every man child in every generation circumcised at eight days, and the uncircumcised man child whose flesh is not circumcised cut off from his people, because he has broken the covenant (Genesis 17:10-14). Moses had spent forty years in Midian and had married Zipporah, a daughter of the priest of Midian and not a daughter of Israel, and the son of that house carried no token of the covenant. The Egyptians did not practise it either; they were a nation of uncleanness, and Israel was afterward told plainly not to do after the doings of the land of Egypt where they had dwelt (Leviticus 18:3).

The word he was carrying makes the neglect weigh more. He was to tell Pharaoh that Israel is the Lord’s son, even his firstborn, and that Pharaoh must let that son go to serve him, and if he refused, the Lord would slay Pharaoh’s son, his firstborn (Exodus 4:22-23). Israel was not the first nation created; Israel was the first nation the Most High chose, the apple of his eye from Abraham, Isaac and Jacob down, and the firstborn is the heir. Moses was going to demand another man’s firstborn on pain of death while his own son bore no token of the very covenant he was invoking. That is why he was worthy of death.
judgmentFull: By the way in the inn, the Lord met him and sought to kill him (Exodus 4:24). Zipporah took a sharp stone and cut off the foreskin of her son and cast it at his feet, and called him a bloody husband; so the Lord let him go, and she said again that he was a bloody husband because of the circumcision (Exodus 4:25-26). Bloody because she had to take the stone and do it herself. The thing had to be set right in his own house before he could carry a word from God into Pharaoh’s house.

This shows the laws did not begin at Sinai, and the covenant still stands. A son of Israel is circumcised on the eighth day (Leviticus 12:3), and a man who comes to the truth grown is still circumcised at forty, fifty or sixty years, as Abraham himself was circumcised at ninety and nine, and as Paul took Timothy, whose father was a Greek, and circumcised him (Genesis 17:24; Acts 16:3). Joshua had to circumcise again the generation born in the wilderness before they took the land (Joshua 5:2-5). Romans does not do away with circumcision of the flesh: circumcision profits if a man keeps the law, and the man circumcised who breaks the law has made his circumcision uncircumcision, while the uncircumcised who keeps the righteousness of the law is counted for circumcision (Romans 2:25-29). The circumcision of the heart is commanded alongside it and not instead of it, Israel being told to circumcise themselves to the Lord and take away the foreskins of their heart (Jeremiah 4:4; Deuteronomy 10:16). Nothing that defiles enters the kingdom (Revelation 21:27).

lawsResolved.text: All male children born are to be circumcised on the eighth day after birth.

text.text: This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, between me and you and thy seed after thee; Every man child among you shall be circumcised.
And ye shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin; and it shall be a token of the covenant betwixt me and you.
And he that is eight days old shall be circumcised among you, every man child in your generations, he that is born in the house, or bought with money of any stranger, which is not of thy seed.
He that is born in thy house, and he that is bought with thy money, must needs be circumcised: and my covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.
And the uncircumcised man child whose flesh of his foreskin is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people; he hath broken my covenant.
After the doings of the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt, shall ye not do: and after the doings of the land of Canaan, whither I bring you, shall ye not do: neither shall ye walk in their ordinances.
And thou shalt say unto Pharaoh, Thus saith the Lord, Israel is my son, even my firstborn:
And I say unto thee, Let my son go, that he may serve me: and if thou refuse to let him go, behold, I will slay thy son, even thy firstborn.
And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that the Lord met him, and sought to kill him.
Then Zipporah took a sharp stone, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet, and said, Surely a bloody husband art thou to me.
So he let him go: then she said, A bloody husband thou art, because of the circumcision.
And in the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.
And Abraham was ninety years old and nine, when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
Him would Paul have to go forth with him; and took and circumcised him because of the Jews which were in those quarters: for they knew all that his father was a Greek.
At that time the Lord said unto Joshua, Make thee sharp knives, and circumcise again the children of Israel the second time.
And Joshua made him sharp knives, and circumcised the children of Israel at the hill of the foreskins.
And this is the cause why Joshua did circumcise: All the people that came out of Egypt, that were males, even all the men of war, died in the wilderness by the way, after they came out of Egypt.
Now all the people that came out were circumcised: but all the people that were born in the wilderness by the way as they came forth out of Egypt, them they had not circumcised.
For circumcision verily profiteth, if thou keep the law: but if thou be a breaker of the law, thy circumcision is made uncircumcision.
Therefore if the uncircumcision keep the righteousness of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision?
And shall not uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfil the law, judge thee, who by the letter and circumcision dost transgress the law?
For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision, which is outward in the flesh:
But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.

Circumcise yourselves to the Lord, and take away the foreskins of your heart, ye men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem: lest my fury come forth like fire, and burn that none can quench it, because of the evil of your doings.
Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked.
And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life.
